red.meaning: A password like that falls in seconds to a guessing program, as shown above. If it's used on more than one account, every one of them opens with it.
red.pro: Fix it with a password manager and a different password per account; our password guides show how. Then Incognito Pro's URL Safety Checker reads a link before you tap it, so you can spot a fake login page first.
red.button: Check links before you log in, with Pro

amber.meaning: That holds out for the time shown above against a guessing program. Make it longer and it holds out far longer: length does more than odd characters.
amber.pro: A stronger password still gets typed wherever a link sends you. Incognito Pro's URL Safety Checker reads the link first, so you can spot a fake login page before you use it there.
amber.button: Check the link first, with Pro

green.meaning: That would take a guessing program decades or more, as shown above. The likelier way it gets stolen now is you typing it into a page that only looks like the real login.
green.pro: Incognito Pro's URL Safety Checker reads a link for look-alike brand names, raw addresses and link shorteners before you tap it, so you can keep that password for the real site.
green.button: Check every login link with Pro
